faqs.question: How do I change my Wi-Fi password?
faqs.answer: Access your router's IP via a browser (usually 192.168.1.1). For a guided walkthrough, contact our WhatsApp support — an agent can help you step-by-step or do it remotely.

faqs.question: What if the router light is red (LOS)?
faqs.answer: A red LOS light means no optical signal. Check that the yellow fiber cable is firmly connected and not sharply bent. If it persists, there may be a fiber cut — report it to our support team.

faqs.question: How do I get an invoice copy?
faqs.answer: Log into the Subscriber Portal with your ID to download invoices or get payment codes. You can also request one instantly via our WhatsApp bot.

faqs.question: How long does installation take?
faqs.answer: Once your contract is approved, installation typically happens within 48 business hours, subject to availability in your area.

faqs.question: Can I change my plan?
faqs.answer: Upgrades are available anytime at no extra cost. Downgrades may require the current billing cycle to close. Contact Sales to manage the change.

faqs.question: Is the speed guaranteed?
faqs.answer: We guarantee 100% of contracted speed via Ethernet (wired) connection. Wi-Fi speeds vary based on interference, router distance, and device limitations.

faqs.question: What if my internet is slow?
faqs.answer: First, restart your router (unplug for 10 seconds). Then test speed using a network cable. If the issue continues, contact our technical team.

faqs.question: How do I schedule a technical visit?
faqs.answer: Schedule via our Official WhatsApp or call center. A technician will first run a remote diagnosis to try resolving the issue before dispatching a visit.

privacidadePage.title: Privacy Policy
privacidadePage.subtitle: How we protect your information.
privacidadePage.intro: Maluga Telecom Sociedad Anonima (RUC 80165701-6), hereinafter referred to as "Maluga Telecom" or simply "We", is committed to protecting the privacy and personal data of its customers, users and visitors of the website https://www.maluga.com.py.
privacidadePage.introLegal: This Privacy Policy was prepared in strict compliance with the legislation of the Republic of Paraguay, including the National Constitution of Paraguay (Art. 135 - Habeas Data), Law No. 4868/13 on Electronic Commerce, Law No. 6534/20 on Personal Data Protection and the current regulations of the National Telecommunications Commission (CONATEL).
privacidadePage.s1Intro: To provide our fiber optic internet services (Basic, Family, Gamer and Business plans) and ensure the best experience on our website, we collect the following types of data:
privacidadePage.s1aTitle: 1.1. Data Provided Directly by the User
s1aItems: Registration Data: Full name, Identity Card (C.I.) or RUC, full address (for installation), email address and phone/WhatsApp number.
Financial Data: Billing information, payment methods and transaction history, necessary for contracting and maintaining plans.
Service Data: Information provided when contacting our Technical Support via WhatsApp, phone or through the Customer Center.
privacidadePage.s1bIntro: As an Internet Service Provider (ISP), we are required to collect certain technical information for service provision and legal compliance:
s1bItems: Connection Logs: Assigned IP addresses, connection dates and times, and traffic volume, as required by CONATEL regulations and Paraguayan data retention laws.
Website Browsing Data: Cookies, browser type, operating system and pages visited on maluga.com.py, aimed at improving our services and platform security.
privacidadePage.s2Intro: Maluga Telecom uses your personal data for the following strict purposes:
s2Items: Service Provision: Enable the installation, configuration and supply of internet connectivity at your home or business.
Commercial Management and Billing: Process payments, issue invoices and manage your account status.
Support and Communication: Handle technical calls (such as Wi-Fi problems, latency or router configuration), send network maintenance alerts and payment due notices.
Legal Obligations: Retain connection records for the period stipulated in Paraguayan law to cooperate with competent authorities in case of official investigations, when there is a court order.
privacidadePage.s3Intro: Maluga Telecom does not sell your personal data to third parties. Sharing only occurs in the following situations:
s3Items: Service Providers: With partner companies that process payments and customer management systems (ERP), under strict confidentiality contracts.
Credit Bureaus: In case of default, information may be reported to credit information agencies (such as Equifax/Informconf), in full compliance with Law No. 6534/20.

Legal and Judicial Authorities: We will provide data, such as connection IP logs, to the Public Prosecutor, National Police or the Judiciary of Paraguay solely and exclusively upon prior and formal court order.
privacidadePage.s4Intro: Under Art. 135 of the National Constitution of Paraguay, you have the right of Habeas Data. This means you can:
s4Items: Access: Request information about which of your data is in our possession.
Rectify: Correct incorrect, inaccurate or outdated data.
Update/Delete: Request the removal of your data when it is no longer necessary for the fulfillment of legal, contractual or regulatory obligations.
privacidadePage.s4Outro: To exercise your rights, contact us through our Customer Service Center.
privacidadePage.s5Text: Our website uses essential cookies to ensure the platform functions (e.g., access to the Customer Center) and analytical cookies to understand how visitors interact with our pages. You can configure your browser to block these cookies, but some website features may be affected.
privacidadePage.s6Text: We adopt the best practices in the telecommunications industry to protect your data, including end-to-end encryption, firewalls and strict server access control. We guarantee the integrity and confidentiality of data transiting our infrastructure.
privacidadePage.s7Text: We will keep your personal data for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes described in this Policy, or for the period required by tax laws and CONATEL regulations for ISPs operating in Paraguayan territory.
privacidadePage.s8Intro: If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or how we handle your data, contact us:
s8Items: WhatsApp: Available through the links on our website.
Headquarters: Agency located in Paraguay (check the exact address at our center).

blogPage.articleTitle: 5 Connectivity Tips to Improve Your Wi-Fi!
blogPage.intro1: Have you ever felt that your internet is not performing as expected, even with a great plan? Most of the time, the problem is not the speed reaching your home, but rather how the Wi-Fi signal is being distributed throughout the rooms.
blogPage.intro2: To help you get the most out of your connection, our technical team has put together 5 simple and easy tips to apply today:
blogPage.tip1Title: 1. Router placement makes all the difference
blogPage.tip1Desc: The biggest mistake is hiding the router inside cabinets, drawers, behind the TV, or on the floor. Wi-Fi signal propagates through the air in waves. Therefore, place the device in a central location in the house, preferably in a high position free from physical obstacles.
blogPage.tip2Desc: Did you know that some appliances can interfere with your Wi-Fi? Microwave ovens, old cordless phones, baby monitors, and even large mirrors or aquariums can weaken the signal. Keep your router away from them.
blogPage.tip3Desc: The vast majority of modern routers transmit the signal on two networks:
blogPage.tip3Bullet1Desc: Offers maximum speed, ideal for high-resolution videos and games, but has a shorter range. It is ideal for use in the same room as the router.
blogPage.tip3Bullet2Desc: It is a bit slower, but the signal travels much further and passes through walls more easily. It is the best option for more distant rooms.
blogPage.tip4Desc: Just like a phone or computer, the router also accumulates processes. Unplugging it, waiting 30 seconds, and plugging it back in helps clear the memory and can instantly resolve freezes and slowdowns.
blogPage.tip5Desc: Unused old phones, Smart TVs plugged in but turned off, and tablets in the drawer may be consuming your internet with background updates. Disconnect devices you do not use frequently from Wi-Fi!
blogPage.conclusion: If even after applying these tips you feel you need more speed to meet the whole family's demand, talk to the Maluga team and discover our ultra-speed plans!

blogPost2.title: Slow Internet or Small Plan? Discover the Truth
blogPost2.p1:
You sit on the couch to watch that 4K series and... the dreaded "loading wheel" appears. The first thing that comes to mind is: "My internet is slow!".
But is it really the signal's fault, or has your internet plan simply become too small for your home?
blogPost2.p2: In the thousands of network installations and maintenance performed daily, a pattern repeats itself: customers often believe that the internet is failing, when in fact, the mathematics of consumption simply don't add up. Understand why.
blogPost2.sub1: The Mathematics of Devices: Internet is Divided
blogPost2.sub1p: Stop and count: how many devices are connected to your Wi-Fi right now? The list is usually larger than we imagine:
blogPost2.sub1li2: Smart TVs in the living room and bedroom;
blogPost2.sub1li5: Smart home devices (light bulbs, smart plugs, and virtual assistants).
blogPost2.sub1p2: The golden rule of connectivity is that your internet is not multiplied, it is divided. If you have a 100 Mega plan and 10 connected devices doing heavy downloads or consuming videos, each one receives only a small slice of that "cake".
blogPost2.sub2p: The way you and your family use the network directly determines the bandwidth requirement. Evaluate which scenario your home fits into:
blogPost2.sub2li1: Basic Use: Text messaging, scrolling through social media feeds, and reading emails. For this profile, more modest plans do the job without hiccups.
blogPost2.sub2li2: Intense Use: Constant work with heavy files in the cloud, video call meetings, competitive online gaming, or high-resolution streaming. Here, broadband demand explodes and requires much more robust plans.
blogPost2.sub3: The Litmus Test: How to be sure?
blogPost2.sub3p: Before getting frustrated with the connection, do the ultimate test. Turn off your computer's Wi-Fi, connect it directly to the router using a network cable, and measure the speed on a reliable site.
blogPost2.sub3p2: Is the contracted speed arriving perfectly via cable, but the Wi-Fi starts to stutter exactly when the whole family arrives home and connects their phones? The diagnosis is clear: your internet plan has become too small for your reality.
blogPost2.sub4: Technology evolves, and your internet needs to keep up
blogPost2.sub4p: Our need for speed grows every day. There is no point in having a latest-generation Smart TV — a true "Ferrari" — and trying to run it on a "dirt road" connection.
blogPost2.sub5: And in your home, how is that math?
blogPost2.sub5p: Take an inventory of how many devices are connected today. If you discovered that it's time for an upgrade, contact your internet provider and ensure a connection that keeps up with your pace!

blogPost3.title: Protect your Wi-Fi Network: Secure Connection
blogPost3.p1: Leaving your Wi-Fi network unprotected or with a very simple password is like leaving home and leaving the front door ajar. A vulnerable network brings two major problems:
blogPost3.li1: Slower internet: Allows neighbors to "hitch a ride" on your bandwidth.
blogPost3.li2: Privacy risks: Exposes your personal data and banking information to malicious people.
blogPost3.p2: Ensuring the digital security of your home is fundamental. Follow these simple steps recommended by our technicians to shield your connection:
blogPost3.sub1: 1. Change the password and network name (SSID)
blogPost3.sub1li1: Create a strong password: Never keep the default password that comes from the factory stuck to the equipment. Use a combination of uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and symbols (@, #, !, etc.).
blogPost3.sub1li2: Protect your identity: When choosing the name of your Wi-Fi network, avoid using personal information such as your full name, phone number, or your apartment number.
blogPost3.sub2li1: Don't share your main password: Are you hosting an event and having friends over? Most routers allow you to create a Guest Network.
blogPost3.sub2li2: Isolate your data: This way, your guests access the internet perfectly, but are isolated from your private network, without access to your connected private devices (like computers and cameras).
blogPost3.sub3li1: Updates are essential: Security also starts on your devices. Always keep your mobile's, computer's operating system, and antivirus updated.
blogPost3.sub3li2: Avoid local contaminations: Threats often spread through an already infected device that connects to your home network.
blogPost3.sub4p: Your online security is our priority. If you need help changing your network data or safely changing your Wi-Fi password, Maluga's technical support is available.

blogPost4.title: Internet for Gamers: The Secret to Playing without Lag
blogPost4.p1: For those who take online gaming seriously — whether on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, or even Mobile —, having a package with a very high download speed is not the only factor that matters for victory. After all, nothing is more frustrating than the dreaded lag: those connection stutters that make characters "teleport" and cause you to lose a decisive match.
blogPost4.p2: In the competitive gaming world (like Valorant, CS, EA FC, League of Legends, or Free Fire), the secret to success goes by two names: Low Ping (Latency) and Stability.
blogPost4.p3: Ping is nothing more than response time. It is the milliseconds that a click on your controller takes to reach the game server and the response to return to your screen.
blogPost4.p4: See how to configure your network environment to play like a true Pro-Player:
blogPost4.sub1: 1. The Network Cable is mandatory for PCs and Consoles
blogPost4.sub1p: This is the golden rule of the Technician's Tips for gamers. Wi-Fi is excellent for videos and social networks, but it suffers invisible micro-interferences through the air all the time.
blogPost4.sub1li: The Solution: If you want to play at the highest level of precision, connect your console or PC directly to the router using a good network cable. The improvement in ping stability is instantaneous.
blogPost4.sub2: 2. Playing on Mobile? Prioritize the 5GHz network
blogPost4.sub2p: Do you play primarily on mobile and have no way to use a cable? No problem, but adjust your connection.
blogPost4.sub2li: The Solution: Ensure your smartphone is connected to the 5GHz Wi-Fi network and play as close as possible to where the router is installed. This frequency processes data much faster and free of interference over short distances.
blogPost4.sub3p: Your network can be congested without you realizing it. If someone in the house is watching 4K movies simultaneously, your connection will inevitably suffer fluctuations during the match.
blogPost4.sub3li: The Solution: Before opening the game, make sure platforms (like Steam, Epic Games, or automatic Windows updates) are not doing heavy and silent downloads in the background.
blogPost4.sub4p: To have the lowest latency on the market, internet technology makes all the difference. Fiber Optic routes suffer very little external interference and deliver data packets at the speed of light, guaranteeing the ideal response time to dominate the servers.
blogPost4.sub5p1: Tired of losing matches due to a bad connection? Maluga's high-performance network delivers the stability and low ping that the most demanding gamers need.
blogPost4.sub5p2: Contact our support and upgrade your setup today!
